Subject: Re: Redwood marketplace onboarding + PO flow

Hi Maya — thanks for the packet and for outlining procurement's requirement. Quick summary of how we can proceed and a few clarifying questions below.

1) Marketplace billing: Redwood supports both marketplace-managed billing (we can be listed and billed via AWS/Azure/GCP marketplaces) and direct invoicing to customers. Accepting a Marketplace-generated PO is usually the faster path because it maps to the marketplace SKU and the PO is reconciled by the marketplace.

2) Exceptions: If procurement requires a single consolidated PO and needs a specific billing entity or tax treatment, we occasionally route a direct PO to finance and record it as a marketplace transaction on our side. That path can introduce a small delay (ordering + accounting approval).

Action items / asks for your team:
- Can you share the exact PO fields your AP system requires (PO number format, fiscal address, tax ID)? The sample_po.xlsx helps but a short list will speed review.
- Please confirm whether the PO must reference a marketplace SKU or can reference a contract/order #: that matters for reconciliation.

Cc'ing Laura from Legal/Finance to review the attached onboarding packet and confirm acceptance criteria. We'll also open a partner support case with AWS to confirm any partner-side steps.

Attachments: Marketplace_PO_Template.xlsx (our suggested mapping)

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick 20-min sync if helpful.

— Rohan Mehta
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rohan_mehta@redwood.com

Thanks Rohan — quick answers below and attaching our signed vendor W-9 and internal guidance.

- PO format: 8-digit numeric, always prefixed with CR- (e.g., CR-00012345).
- Required fields: PO number, vendor legal name, vendor tax ID (EIN), remit-to address, marketplace listing code (if billing via AWS).
- The PO should reference the marketplace SKU when possible; if not available, include Redwood contract ref (we can add that to our Purchase Order workflow).

We prefer marketplace-managed billing, but procurement will accept direct invoicing if we supply a consolidated PO and internal approval note explaining why (fastest route is marketplace though).

Attachments: SignedW9.pdf

Would like to close onboarding this week — do you have availability Wednesday or Thursday for 20 min?

Best,
Maya

Subject: Internal: recommended PO paths + quick playbook for Cloud Retailer

Team — after reviewing Maya's packet and the SignedW9, here are two recommended paths and risks so we can advise the customer clearly:

Path A (preferred): Marketplace-managed billing (AWS/Azure/GCP).
- Pros: fastest procurement approval, standardized reconciliation (marketplace SKU in PO), no special invoicing from Redwood.
- Cons: our finance team needs marketplace listing code and to ensure correct remit mapping.

Path B (fallback): Direct consolidated PO to Redwood finance.
- Pros: satisfies customer billing system exactly.
- Cons: requires manual accounting entry and an internal SLA exception; may delay invoice issuance by 3–5 business days.

Recommended next steps (short checklist):
- Rohan: confirm PO sample fields with Maya (they've provided format; we added mapping in Marketplace_PO_Template.xlsx).
- Laura: confirm whether Redwood can accept CR-prefixed PO numbers and whether tax ID mapping requires a subsidiary-level remit.
- Ops: open a partner-support ticket with AWS to verify listing code propagation (I can do this; will loop in AWS Partner Support).

I've attached a lightweight workflow diagram that we can share with Maya highlighting the two options. If procurement insists on direct PO, we should prepare the SLA exception request now so it doesn't block go-live.

Attachments: marketplace_workflow_diagram.png

— Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com

2) Vanessa opened an AWS partner ticket to confirm listing code propagation; partner support estimated 24–48 hours for confirmation.
3) If marketplace-managed billing is acceptable, we can list and go live once AWS confirms the SKU mapping. Estimated time: 2 business days after partner confirmation.
4) If procurement requires a direct consolidated PO, we can accept it but will file an internal SLA exception; estimated lead time: 5 business days for invoicing and reconciliation.
